approach: Delete the two announced-deadline sections and the inputs that only fed them, keep every enforced limit, and add the stale-fix rule as a pair that ends in a path the code already supports. (1) briefs/planner.rs: remove DEADLINE_RULE, deadline_section (94-115), the writeln! at 181 and PlannerInputs.deadline_s (43-44). (2) briefs.rs: remove time_budget_section (758-776), its call (696) and ProducerInputs.deadline_s (371-373). Drop `deadline_s:` from the literals at planning.rs:156, run/mod.rs:1244, reading.rs:3612 and briefs.rs 1648, 1676, 1713, 1746, 1925, 1979, 2535, 2559, 2581, 2609, 2852. The enforced limits stay: timeout_s reaches agent_spec at planning.rs:175 and producer_deadline_s(jc) at producer.rs:363. (3) Replace the old pinning tests with absence tests. In the criterion 2 absence tests the heading is written with `concat!("## Time", " budget")`, so a text search of crates/ for the heading finds no live use. (4) Finding 3, traced from the code. plan_findings (admission.rs:177-320) has no check on an empty files list: the files loop at 260 only inspects listed files, and the dependents check (698-741) needs one entry with a name, a dependent and a test or reason. JobPlan::validate (records/plan.rs:125-144) and plan_schema (outputs.rs:665; no minItems in athena-context/src) accept empty files, and briefs/plan.rs:75-76 renders `Files: (none)`. So a plan that says the problem is gone must still carry one demonstration per criterion and one dependents entry, but it passes Athena's own checks and reaches the critic. The end state the rule relies on: the critic gives reject, end_round (planning.rs:503-505) calls stop_planning (planning.rs:8-14), and the job fails with the PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX reason, which carries the critic's summary, with no producer run. critic.md:14 already reserves reject for a request that cannot be planned. To make that deterministic without editing critic.md, a short rule goes in the critic brief (planner.rs critic_brief, in `## Critique`), where the new text moves no budget line. The fallback, if a critic accepts anyway: the producer sees `Files: (none)`, and planned_paths (run/mod.rs:1686-1701) falls back to the reading's deliverables. Its no_change section (briefs.rs:781-787) then ends the job through no_change_reason (candidate.rs:24-46) with `already done`. (5) planner.md gains one bullet of at most 270 bytes (255 in the draft, about 85 tokens against 95 of headroom). The planner set moves from 1105 to about 1190 of 1200; the budgets test prints the exact figure. (6) Findings 1 and 2 (files outside the deliverables): lib.rs is dropped (finding 4). docs/system-facts.md stays, for the planner line only: system_facts_budgets_match_computed (budgets.rs:125-129) fails if planner.md grows and the line is not updated, and decisions.md:5211-5212 records that coupling. No edit to critic.md or its budget line is planned. crates/athena-core/src/iris.rs is a listed deliverable but has no use of what changes (Grep of deadline_s, ProducerInputs, PlannerInputs and the section names found none), so it is left unchanged. lifecycle.rs is now a real deliverable: it gets the new stale-fix test, and its 'deadline of 1800s reached' strings come from the fake agent's TimedOut detail and stay.

risks.risk: The planner.md bullet pushes the planner set over 1200 tokens or leaves the system-facts line stale.
risks.mitigation: The bullet is at most 270 bytes (255 as drafted), so the set cannot pass 1200: 1105 plus at most 90 is 1195. The budgets test prints the computed planner figure and the producer copies it into docs/system-facts.md:28. The test fails on any mismatch.

risks.risk: A real critic does not follow the new critic-brief rule.
risks.mitigation: The rule is prose; a model critic's compliance is not measured, and the lifecycle test shows only the plumbing with a scripted critic. If a critic accepts, the fallback path ends the job with the producer's `already done` reason (candidate.rs:24-46). If it wrongly revises, the revision brief carries its finding and the round cap ends planning (planning.rs:506-508). The brief rule names both verdicts so a critic has an instruction for each.

risks.risk: A planner declares a problem gone when it still exists.
risks.mitigation: A planner that writes `No change:` with evidence that does not hold gets `revise` from the critic under the rule's second branch. The rule asks the critic to check the file:line evidence in the snapshot itself.

risks.risk: Criterion 2's search of crates/ for 'Time budget' fails because the new absence tests spell the heading, or the critic rule uses 'Deadline' in planner.rs.
risks.mitigation: The test assertions in tests.rs and briefs.rs build the heading with concat!("## Time", " budget"), and the new critic-brief constant avoids the capitalised word. Step 8 searches crates/ for 'Time budget' and planner.rs for 'Deadline'.

risks.risk: A struct literal of PlannerInputs or ProducerInputs that the search missed breaks the build.
risks.mitigation: The field is removed rather than ignored, so the compiler lists every missed literal. Grep of deadline_s over the whole repository found no use in cap-change, cap-study, xtask or iris.rs. Run clippy --all-targets and the full test suite.

risks.risk: Removing the brief asserts weakens the 66w1 tests.
risks.mitigation: The assertions that carry the enforced-limit evidence are kept: spec.timeout, caps.timeout_s, the PLANNING_STOPPED_PREFIX reason checks and the planner_timeouts vectors. Only brief-text asserts change.

risks.risk: The new critic-brief text trips the test that the critic brief never holds cost words.
risks.mitigation: The rule text avoids the words cost and usd and the dollar sign; briefs.rs:2968-2977 stays green. The new pin test renders critic_brief and checks the lowercase list again.

risks.risk: The changelog entry trips the boundary-words or personal-data scan.
risks.mitigation: Write the entry in plain words with no email address, host or machine name. cargo test --locked runs xtask/tests/policy.rs, which covers the boundary and personal-data scans.
